title: ProgressBar time column: use rich task.finished_time, not task.elapsed, for finished tasks
answers: progress bar timer keeps running after bar is full
finished sub-estimator bar elapsed time keeps increasing in meta-estimator
ProgressBar max_propagation_depth timers wrong for completed tasks
which rich Task attribute gives frozen elapsed time
body:
Symptom: when you use the ProgressBar callback with max_propagation_depth > 0 on a meta-estimator, bars that are already full keep counting up their elapsed time while later sibling bars fill.
Root cause: sklearn/callback/_progressbar.py:render (the custom rich time column with `elapsed_when_finished`) read `task.elapsed`. A rich Task counts as `finished` once completed reaches total, but `elapsed` keeps measuring against the current clock until the task is explicitly stopped.
Fix pattern: for finished tasks, display `task.finished_time`. Rich freezes this value when the task completes. Unfinished tasks still show `task.time_remaining`.
Constraints: this applies to any rich column or rendering code in the callback module that shows a duration for a completed task. Don't depend on `task.elapsed` being frozen unless the code calls `stop_task` explicitly.
